bullets.title: Fed hiked 25bp; dot plot signals at least one more hike, terminal rate just above 4%
bullets.body: The Fed raised rates 25bp to 3.75-4.0% at the Sept 18 meeting; 16 of 18 dots signal at least one additional hike, with the dot plot coalescing around a terminal rate just above 4%. Chair Warsh indicated the FOMC would be 'hard-pressed' to call conditions restrictive, leaving room for further tightening. Markets now price ~55% odds of an October hike and ~34bp of additional hikes through year-end.

bullets.title: Labor market re-accelerating: claims at 196K, wage growth inflecting higher
bullets.body: Initial claims fell to 196K, the first sub-200K print since mid-July and near multi-decade lows; continuing claims dropped to 1.73M, lowest since early 2024 and down ~10% Y/Y. ADP hiring is firming, Indeed job postings set to turn positive post-pandemic, and cyclical industry wage growth is accelerating. PSC Macro corroborates: claims declines lead payrolls by ~2 months and point to rising wage inflation concerns.

bullets.title: 10Y yield at ~4.98%; Hedgeye targets 5.12% cycle high, curve flattening persists
bullets.body: The 10-year Treasury yield rose 5bp to 4.98% in pre-market; Hedgeye's risk range is 4.81-5.12%, with both 2s and 10s signaling higher cycle highs. The 10s-2s curve has flattened by roughly half since August. Hedgeye is positioned to add shorts in TLT, ZROZ, LQD, and XLU on strength, and maintains CCC credit spreads widened above 900bp with borrowing costs for weaker credits approaching ~15%.

bullets.title: Bond yield rise driven by higher real rates (r*), not fiscal risk premiums—but fiscal strain looms
bullets.body: MacDonell argues the recent bond yield surge reflects higher real rates (r*) above nominal growth (g*), not default concerns or inflation expectations. Higher government debt has forced r* up via demand-stimulating safe-asset effects, breaking down the post-COVID 'Ponzi Public Finance' (r*<g*) framework. This raises future fiscal strain risks but does not constitute an immediate crisis signal.

bullets.title: French-German 10Y spread widens to 100bp, widest since 2012; eurozone fiscal stress building
bullets.body: The French-German 10-year yield spread reached 100 basis points, the widest since the 2012 eurozone crisis, as France raised its 2026 deficit forecast to 5.4% and targets 5.0% for 2027 via pension and wage cuts facing a divided parliament. EU Economic Commissioner warns rising bond yields will affect all of Europe and called for stronger fiscal policies. ECB's Lagarde characterized yields as part of a global trend with no chaotic movements, committing to a meeting-by-meeting approach.

bullets.title: Global central banks broadly hawkish: BoE hiking November, ECB March 2027, Norges/Riksbank signaling Q4 hikes
bullets.body: BoE held at 3.75% but signaled a November hike as UK CPI rose to 3.1% with services sticky; JPM expects an additional hike in February 2027, with CPI peaking near 4% by early 2027. JPMorgan now expects the ECB to deliver a 25bp hike in December and another in March 2027. Both Riksbank and Norges Bank are expected to hold next week but shift to explicitly hawkish guidance, with JPM calling for Riksbank hike in December. Hong Kong also raised 25bp to 4.25%.

bullets.title: BoJ hike disappointed on forward guidance; yen weakening sharply
bullets.body: The Bank of Japan raised rates 25bp to the highest level since 1995, but forward guidance on future hikes disappointed markets, sending the yen down over 1% overnight. USD/JPY surged back to the 158 area after whipsawing the critical 155 level. JPM FX technicals flag low conviction on directional calls given messy chart structure.

bullets.title: DXY breaking out to highest since July, on track for 8th consecutive up day
bullets.body: The US Dollar Index hit its highest level since July and is on pace for an eighth straight day without a red close, consistent with tighter global dollar liquidity driven by Fed hawkishness. JPM FX technicals note EUR/USD broke below 1.15 support, shifting focus to 1.12-1.13 medium-term support; AUD/USD forming a potential downside reversal below 0.72 resistance.

bullets.title: Oil WTI falls below $100 for third day; diesel at record $6.45/gallon; Saudi cuts European crude allocations
bullets.body: WTI crude slipped below $100/bbl (-0.52% to $96.72 pre-market) for the third straight session while refined products diverge sharply—US diesel hit a fresh record of $6.45/gallon per AAA data, up 68% year-over-year. Saudi Aramco told European refiners they will receive no crude next month, threatening to widen the diesel supply crisis; Exxon's Joliet refinery disruption adds additional Midwest supply pressure.

bullets.title: Energy Secretary signals possible additional SPR releases; SPR near lowest levels since early 1980s
bullets.body: Energy Secretary Chris Wright called another round of crude loans from the Strategic Petroleum Reserve 'a very real possibility,' citing high prices and steep futures backwardation. Hedgeye notes SPR is near its lowest levels since the early 1980s, adding that Brent physical pricing is running ~$120-125 versus futures, with Red Sea shipping constraints potentially adding $20+/barrel in incremental costs.

bullets.title: Core PCE tracking 3.3% Q4/Q4; inflation expected to re-accelerate and pull October/December hike odds forward
bullets.body: 22V Research tracks core PCE at 3.3% Q4/Q4 2026, well above the 2% target. MS revised core PCE higher to 3.2% for 4Q/4Q 2026 and 2.7% for 4Q/4Q 2027, citing persistent energy cost pressures and firms shifting their perception of energy costs from temporary to permanent. Hedgeye expects the next inflation print to accelerate, pulling rate-hike expectations to October or December and subsequently slowing GDP growth roughly in half.

bullets.title: August industrial production flat; manufacturing down 0.3%, semis tick lower but comms equipment at record
bullets.body: August industrial production was flat month-over-month versus a +0.3% consensus estimate; manufacturing declined 0.3% m/m with vehicle production down a second straight month. AI-related industrial demand softened after April-July strength, though communications equipment remains in a strong uptrend at record highs. Philadelphia Fed Manufacturing Index (ISM-adjusted) ticked down to 58.3 but remains in expansion territory; 68% of surveyed manufacturers expect higher 3Q production.

bullets.title: S301 tariff legal challenge: CIT hearing Sept 30 with ~$100B refund risk if invalidated
bullets.body: The Court of International Trade will hear arguments September 30 on challenges to Trump's new Section 301 tariffs applied globally to 60 economies covering 99% of US imports at 10-12.5% rates, projected to raise ~$1 trillion over 10 years. Challengers argue the Administration exceeded legal authority; a ruling similar to the IEEPA invalidation (which generated $170B in refunds) could produce ~$100B in refunds and negatively affect the bond market via fiscal revenue concerns.

bullets.title: Trump-Xi meeting Sept 24 is the major geopolitical focal point; rare earth deal expiry Nov 10 key item
bullets.body: The Trump-Xi summit is scheduled for September 24 at the White House, with deliverables under discussion including a US-China Board of Trade, purchase commitments, advanced technology expansion, and Taiwan. The rare earth and critical mineral deal expires November 10 and its extension is a key negotiation item alongside tech export controls and tariff agenda. Raymond James and Morgan Stanley both flagging this as a market focal point.

bullets.title: TX governor race tightening: data center regulatory risk rising if Hinojosa wins
bullets.body: New polls show Hinojosa potentially leading Abbott in the Texas governor's race for the first time. Hinojosa has previously pushed for data center moratoriums and ending tax breaks; a win would mark a significant shift in what has been a pro-data center regulatory environment in a critical power and land market for AI infrastructure.

bullets.title: Democrats now favored to take back both Senate (60%) and House (90%) per Polymarket
bullets.body: Polymarket odds show Democrats at 60% to reclaim the Senate and 90% to take back the House. Morgan Stanley is hosting a midterm elections webcast covering fiscal scenarios and growth implications, noting positioning and execution considerations into November as a key investor focus.

bullets.title: AI adoption at 47.8% of S&P 1500; early adopters maintain margin edge, broader adoption diluting benefits
bullets.body: AI adoption across S&P 1500 companies rose from 16.8% in 1Q23 to 47.8% in 2Q26, but early adopters maintain materially higher and more stable margins than newer entrants who face upfront costs before productivity gains materialize. 22V notes AI Services and AI Buildout run at -80% rolling correlation but expects macro backdrop of mild tightening to push convergence. The AI productivity/disinflationary boom thesis has not yet materialized in aggregate employment or margin data.

bullets.title: GPU rental prices rising 17-21%; power costs at $40M/MW; compute shortage remains key investable theme
bullets.body: Nebius and CoreWeave raised GPU rental prices 17-21% starting October 1, with short-term power contracts running ~$40M per megawatt in an extremely tight market. Hopper GPU rental prices also up 3% m/m per Raymond James token data. No data center project pauses or cancellations reported across five companies tracked by 22V; liquid cooling content per MW doubled to $3.4M with CMI order books extending to 2H28.

bullets.title: Anthropic and OpenAI pivoting to smaller 20-30MW data center deals for faster capacity deployment
bullets.body: Anthropic and OpenAI are pursuing smaller 20-30MW data center deals in markets including the UK and Nordics, prioritizing speed to usable capacity over large-scale single-site builds. Anthropic targets 5GW total capacity by year-end 2026 and 10GW by year-end 2027. CoreWeave separately increased its convertible notes offering to $3.7B from $3.0B.

bullets.title: Semiconductor inventory flashing yellow: 58 days, up 12 days over 3 quarters; datacenter demand offsets concern
bullets.body: Aggregate semiconductor customer end-market inventory increased 4 days q/q to ~58 days in 2Q following a 3-day rise in 1Q; on a dollar basis, inventory rose ~16% q/q and +52% y/y. Inventory remains below the prior 62-day peak and the yellow flag is tempered by strong datacenter demand visibility, rising memory prices, and AI demand anticipation. Wolfe notes inventory is one of the most important cyclical indicators for the sector.
